questions.q: Why is tampering with the blockchain nearly impossible?
a: Each block carries the previous block's data and must match the network
A central bank verifies every new block by hand
Blocks are protected by passwords known only to miners
Old transactions are deleted once they are confirmed
questions.why: The linked blocks and consensus process mean everything must line up perfectly.

questions.q: What do Bitcoin miners compete to do?
a: Solve complex math problems to add blocks and earn cryptocurrency
Approve new users before they can open a wallet
Set the exchange rate for each transaction
Store copies of every wallet on their own servers
questions.why: Proof of work relies on computational effort to keep records accurate without a central authority.

questions.q: Why does the summary call the current banking system unequal?
a: Small payments are unprofitable, leaving billions without accounts
Banks charge wealthy customers higher fees
Online banking is unavailable in most countries
Only governments can open a bank account
questions.why: A payment under 20 cents is not worth processing, yet billions live on less than a dollar a day.

questions.q: How could a government use blockchain to show taxpayers where money goes?
a: By using one identifiable signature that the public can track
By publishing all transactions under a secret key
By allowing only auditors to view the records
By deleting spending records after each year
questions.why: A consistent signature lets the public follow spending and trust the institution.

questions.q: What are smart contracts used for in the summary?
a: Choosing which data to share and which to keep private
Automatically raising prices when demand is high
Replacing lawyers in property transactions
Verifying that a miner solved a math problem
questions.why: They let users grant temporary, selective access, such as showing a police officer clean records.
